source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_documented.growth_habit: Annual herb 15–30 cm tall (annual from historical Valerianella genus)
morphology_documented.stems: Glabrous stem; leaf bases can bear paired hair tufts (genus key)
morphology_documented.leaves: Simple, opposite, sessile except lowest, often clasping, entire or with few basal teeth/lobes (genus)
morphology_documented.flowers: Small head-like leafy-bracted terminal cymes; flowers relatively conspicuous, many open together and overtop small bracts; white funnel-shaped corollas 3–4.5 mm across
morphology_documented.fruit: Dry one-seeded fruits usually <3 mm long (genus); two sterile locules much smaller than fertile locule; shallow narrow or inconspicuous intervening groove; key describes broad ovate to round fruits with minute hooked hairs
morphology_documented.habitat: Bare limestone outcrops, Austin Chalk Blackland Prairie

source_scope_note: Species vs. genus or key-level characters distinguished in each entry. No missing traits inferred.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Historical family Valerianaceae, current Caprifoliaceae; historical genus Valerianella is accepted as Valeriana in current POWO species concept
Flora's fruit characters require actual mature fruit to confirm, not inferred from flowers
preservation: Additive record; original species.json, media, credits and galleries unchanged
